claims.assertion: The driver's chat message at 18:21 asked the rider not to smoke in the car, which is a lawful in-vehicle conduct request and not a provocation that justifies any threat.
The rider's reply at 18:22 — 'Say that again and I will punch you' — is a threat of physical violence directed at the driver, and the keyword flag confirms it ('punch').
The driver's written statement repeats the same threat allegation, so the complaint is not invented after the fact: a threat appears in the in-app record itself.
SAFE-1 requires that a threat of this kind be escalated to human review rather than decided automatically, so a case summary should be sent for manual handling.

The rider has 1,316 days of account history, a 4.5 rating and zero disputes in the last 90 days, so the rider is a long-standing non-abusive user and no account-level flag against the rider is warranted on this record.

With a 4.85 rating over 427 trips and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days, the driver has no history of fee or dispute abuse, supporting that this report is genuine rather than a fee-extraction attempt.

There is no billing dispute in this case that would justify offsetting or retaining any part of the metered fare: the trip ran 8.8 km against an 8.9 km optimal route (-0.1 km) and 13.3 min against a 16 min estimate, i.e. no route deviation.

weaknesses: The threat message F4 exists in the chat log and is corroborated by the keyword flag F5, so the strongest available defence — that the driver misunderstood or fabricated the exchange — is not open to us; the rider's account hands the driver the case.

F3 shows the flashpoint was the rider's own conduct (smoking in the vehicle) after a polite request, which an adjudicator may treat as aggravating rather than mitigating, and there is no chat message in the record showing the rider apologised, retracted, or clarified the threat was a joke.

The driver's statement F6 is a self-serving narrative accepted on its face only because the underlying chat (F4/F5) happens to corroborate it; if the rider gives a competing account, the system-record rule means the rider's version will be subordinated unless the rider produces evidence (e.g. prior good record F7) to counter it.
Nothing in the record shows any prior provocation, harassment or aggressive conduct by the driver (F8 shows a clean 427-trip record), so no counter-mitigation on the driver's side is available to us.

claims.assertion: The rider sent an explicit threat of physical violence in the in-app chat: at 18:22, one minute after the driver's request not to smoke, the rider wrote "Say that again and I will punch you."
The system's own keyword detector independently flagged the rider's message as a threat ('punch') at 18:22, so this is not merely the driver's account of the exchange.
The driver's written statement repeats the same threat and requests that it be reported, and the driver's conduct in the chat was limited to a lawful, polite request not to smoke in the vehicle.

The trip itself shows no irregularity by the driver — actual distance 8.8 km was 0.1 km shorter than the 8.9 km optimal route and the trip finished 3.0 minutes early — confirming the driver took the direct route and the dispute concerns only the rider's conduct.

Threats and intimidation are expressly outside tolerated conduct and require immediate termination and possible legal action, so the correct disposition is referral to human handling rather than an automated fare ruling.

Supporting profile context only: the driver has 732 days of account age, a 4.85 rating, 427 trips in 90 days and zero disputes upheld, while the rider has 0 disputes in 90 days — offered solely as context for the escalation, not as grounds for the finding.

weaknesses: The threat is recorded only in the in-app chat; there is no GPS, timeline or other system record of the physical incident itself, so the finding rests on the chat log (F3, F4) plus the driver's own statement (F6).
The threat was conditional ('Say that again and I will punch you', F4) and no assault or injury is recorded, so the rider may argue no safety incident actually occurred.
Nothing in the case file shows the driver reported the matter via RydeHELP or called 995 at the time, which the other side can use to question the timeliness and seriousness of the complaint (F6).
The driver is the filing party and the account history is clean on both sides (F7, F8), so there is no prior-violation pattern that would support any account action against the rider.

points.response: Conceded as to the words: the chat record shows the rider's message at 18:22 reading 'Say that again and I will punch you' immediately after the driver's 18:21 request not to smoke (F4, F3). We contest only the inference that this makes the rider a safety risk requiring account action — the record shows a single conditional sentence, no assault, and no repeat, and the rider's 1,316-day, 4.5-rating, zero-dispute history gives no pattern for a rider-side flag (F7).

Accepted: the keyword detector flagged 'punch' in message #2 (F5), so the threat is a system-recorded fact, not merely the driver's word. That is exactly why the correct disposition is referral for manual handling under SAFE-1 rather than any automated penalty against the rider.

We accept the driver's 18:21 message was a lawful, polite request not to smoke (F3) and that the statement repeats the allegation (F6), but the timing shows the exchange lasted about one minute and was triggered by the rider's smoking, not by any unprovoked aggression; the record contains no second threat, no escalation and no further messages (F4, F5).

We agree the trip data show no driver-side irregularity — 8.8 km actual against an 8.9 km optimal route and 13.3 min actual against a 16 min estimate (F1, F2) — and we make no route or fare claim against the driver in this case.

We agree SAFE-1 requires escalation rather than an automated ruling and we ask for the same relief; we only ask that the human reviewer's summary record that no physical contact, injury or repeat conduct appears anywhere in the file, so that the escalation is not read as an established history against the rider (F4, F6, F7).

We accept the profile facts as context only (F7, F8); they are admissible as support for an additional action but can never decide this finding, and here they show no upheld violation against either party, so no account flag on the rider is justified (F7).
Conceded — F3 shows the driver's only message was a lawful request not to smoke, and no facts in the record show any provocation by the driver.

Conceded and relied upon: F4 records the rider's threat word-for-word and F5 shows the system's own keyword detector flagged 'punch', so the threat is established on the system record, not merely on testimony.
Conceded — F6 is the driver's statement, but it is corroborated rather than contradicted by the chat record in F4/F5, which is why the report is credible.
Agreed, and this is exactly the driver's requested outcome: SAFE-1 mandates escalate with a fact summary for human handling, not an automatic ruling.
The driver does not seek any flag against the rider's account, so this point is not in dispute; F7 is offered only as context and cannot by itself decide the safety question under SAFE-1.
Accepted — F8 supports that this report is genuine and not an attempt to extract fees, and no fare or fee is contested by the driver in this case.

Conceded — F1 shows the actual distance was 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route and F2 shows the trip finished 3.0 min early, so the driver claims no fare adjustment and the metered fare stands unchanged.
